item.title: The Circularity Gap Report: Critical Raw Materials
item.description: This report examines how the circular economy can reshape the dynamics of critical raw materials by reducing how much material is needed in the first place, extending how long it stays in use, and increasing how much returns to the economy when products reach end of life.

item.title: Decarbonisation is on course to run short of key materials, but circularity could bridge the gap
item.description: Without action, the energy transition could stall for lack of critical raw materials, finds the Circularity Gap Report: Critical Raw Materials , released by Circle Economy in collaboration with Deloitte Netherlands. Under a business-as-usual scenario, copper, silicon, lithium and cobalt would each face more than a decade of supply shortages between now and 2050. However, circular strategies such as efficient design, durability and recycling could help bridge the gap without slowing climate ac...

item.title: The Legacy of COP 31: Circularity Monitoring Platform to track and accelerate progress towards 15% circularity by 2035.
item.description: This Open Letter, initiated by Circle Economy, calls on the COP31 Presidency to establish a Global Circularity Monitoring Platform to track the progress towards a goal of 15% circular material use in the manufacturing and production sectors by 2035.

item.title: Financing a European Circular Transition: From investment-readiness to investment alignment
item.description: If circularity is strategically important to European resilience and competitiveness, financial policy must look beyond investment readiness and private capital mobilisation. It must also address how resource-related risks are assessed, where credit is directed, which activities continue to receive financial support, and when direct public investment or ownership is needed.

item.title: Circular Economy Financing: an Investor Guide
item.description: This document serves as a practical guide for investors engaging with the circular economy. It is intended to be broadly suitable to multiple stages and type of business, and is structured in line with these three key dimensions of the investment case – value, risk and impact – and presents the nuances of circularity in each case, as well as citing the most relevant existing resources, tools and frameworks to be considered.

item.title: The Or Foundation, adidas, BESTSELLER, H&M Group, and Inditex launch Apparel Recovery Coalition, responding to impacts of post-consumer textile exports
item.description: ACCRA, Ghana, September 29—adidas, BESTSELLER, H&M Group, Inditex and The Or Foundation, with support from Circle Economy, unveiled the Apparel Recovery Coalition (ARC). The coalition will explore how producer responsibility systems can support circular pathways such as reuse, upcycling, recycling, and responsible waste management in countries that receive large volumes of exported secondhand apparel.

item.title: The story we tell ourselves about donated clothes is incomplete
item.description: Every year, millions of tonnes of used textiles leave Europe. Exports have tripled since 2000, reaching almost 1.7 million tonnes in 2023 . Nearly half are destined for countries in Africa, while more than 40% are sent to Asia. For many consumers, this is where visibility ends. Yet the global trade in secondhand clothing raises an uncomfortable question: when clothes are reused, are we solving a waste problem, or simply moving responsibility elsewhere?

item.title: Urban Planning for the Circular Economy: a spatial turn in theory and practice
item.description: This white paper contributes to the Circular Cities and Regions Initiative (CCRI), supporting cities and regions in their circular transition. It was produced as part of the Circular Cities and Regions Initiative (CCRI) Communities of Practice (CoP) project, funded under Horizon Europe, enabling peer learning, collaboration, and knowledge exchange across thematic communities.

item.title: A degrowth-oriented circular society: What can circular economy practitioners learn from degrowth research?
item.description: This article is authored by Martin Calisto Friant, Sustainability Scholar and Practitioner and Senior Researcher at Circle Economy. It summarises the latest research on degrowth and provides insights for circular economy practitioners.

item.title: How Doughnut Economics can transform sectors
item.description: This article summarises lessons learned from the Live Labs 2 project, applying Doughtnut Economics to the highways sector in the UK. These lessons form a blueprint for a systemic transformation of any sector.

item.title: Circle City Scan Bogotá
item.description: The Circle City Scan Bogotá-Region (CCS Bogotá-Region) provides a solid evidence base for understanding the city's urban metabolism from a circular economy perspective. Based on environmental footprint analysis, this study estimates the impacts associated with the city's consumption in terms of material use and carbon emissions, offering a comprehensive view of how Bogotá consumes resources and generates environmental impacts throughout its supply chains. The report is in Spanish.

item.title: Closing the gap: How the EU can lead a fair and global circular transition
item.description: The circular economy offers a practical approach to achieving climate stability, resource security, and fair global value chains. But a successful circular transition must work across borders, support workers and communities, and reduce the environmental and socioeconomic pressures created by today’s linear systems.

item.title: Circle Economy’s recommendations for an effective Digital Product Passport for textiles
item.description: The Digital Product Passport (DPP) represents a significant opportunity to improve transparency, traceability, and circularity within the textile sector. Circle Economy, a Dutch think tank specialised in the circular economy transition, welcomes and supports the Joint Research Centre’s (JRC) recommendations for establishing a DPP for textiles.

item.title: Indicators that drive the circular transition
item.description: Circularity indicators are essential for designing impactful policies, but there are many different sets and frameworks to choose from, each capturing circularity in its own way. Not all circularity indicators measure the same thing, and understanding what different metrics capture is essential for designing effective interventions.

item.title: Why circular fashion doesn’t always mean less environmental impact
item.description: Circular solutions in fashion are not inherently impactful. Displacement rates help us to quantify how much consumer behaviour actually contributes to avoided production, helping us understand how effective circular textile solutions are.

item.title: Promoting Sustainable Practices and Worker Protection in Bangladesh’s Jhut Sector: Policy Pathways for a Circular Textile Economy
item.description: This policy brief aims to help both Bangladesh’s national policymakers and international development partners to better understand the country's post-industrial textile waste-processing sector (Jhut) and to design inclusive circular transition policies.

item.title: Food waste to omega-3
item.description: This project based in Norway develops a circular solution that converts food waste into a liquid fermentation medium used to cultivate micro-algae rich in omega-3 oils. The resulting oils are designed to serve as a sustainable alternative to fish oil, which is currently the primary source of omega-3 in aquaculture feed.

item.title: Reducing e-waste through circular device management
item.description: ReNew Lifecycle is a Romanian circular economy solution focused on extending the lifecycle of electronic devices through refurbishment, repair, and intelligent fleet management. The platform serves both businesses and individual users by enabling more efficient management, repair, and reuse of mobile devices and laptops.

item.title: Reducing food waste through B2B surplus trading platforms
item.description: Optifood is a Slovenian B2B digital marketplace designed to reduce food waste by enabling the efficient trading and redistribution of surplus food. The platform connects producers, retailers, and other food system actors, using data analytics and AI to match supply with demand in real time. By creating structured secondary markets for surplus food, Optifood helps businesses recover value from excess inventory while reducing environmental impacts associated with food waste.

item.title: Reusable packaging systems for a circular economy
item.description: Ocean Package is a German circular packaging venture focused on transforming the packaging industry through reusable, closed-loop systems. The company develops and promotes reusable packaging solutions designed to replace single-use formats and reduce waste generation across supply chains.

item.title: Smart charging stations using recycled batteries for cities
item.description: rEcharge is a Slovenian cleantech initiative developing cost-effective, sustainable charging stations for city e-bikes and e-scooters. The system is designed for easy installation and integrates high-capacity battery packs made from recycled lithium-ion cells, supported by IoT connectivity for monitoring, management, and energy provisioning.

item.title: Making reuse as seamless as single-use through POS integration
item.description: Recirculate Systems is a UK-based fintech-enabled circular economy startup that reduces single-use waste by linking reusable products directly to payment transactions. Using RFID technology integrated into point-of-sale (POS) systems, the company enables automated deposit returns and seamless reuse workflows without requiring a consumer-facing app. By embedding reuse into existing payment infrastructure, Recirculate makes reusable packaging and products as convenient as single-use alternatives.

item.title: Advanced dismantling systems for circular material recovery
item.description: REVIRA Technologies is a Portuguese circular technology company developing intelligent dismantling and material detection systems for complex waste streams such as mattresses, foam products, and automotive components. The company enables the recovery of high-quality, traceable secondary raw materials by combining automated dismantling with advanced material identification and digital traceability systems.

item.title: Smart building extension to avoid demolition
item.description: SURLEV is a French construction innovation company pioneering upward building extension through roof lifting techniques that enable additional floors to be added without demolition or expansion of land use. The approach preserves and reuses existing roof structures, reducing material waste while creating new usable urban space within existing building footprints.

item.title: PORTNET
item.description: PORTNET is a Spanish digital solution designed to improve circularity and traceability in maritime waste management. Developed through the Ports 4.0 initiative, the platform uses digital waste passports to connect stakeholders across the maritime value chain, including ships, port authorities, recyclers, and manufacturers. item.title: Turning food waste into high-value functional ingredients
item.description: Simply No Waste is a Swedish startup transforming fruit and vegetable side-streams into functional ingredients for the food, supplement, and cosmetics industries. Using advanced extraction technology and microbial fermentation, the company converts underutilised biological by-products into clean-label, nutrient-rich ingredients that can replace virgin raw materials in a range of commercial applications.

item.title: Upcycling waste materials into modular housing solutions
item.description: Circular Life is a Slovenian initiative focused on upcycling existing materials into functional products and modular housing solutions. The company develops movable container housing units constructed entirely from repurposed materials, reducing the need for virgin resource extraction while extending the lifespan of materials that would otherwise become waste.

item.title: How Re:Lab is creating value from difficult-to-recycle plastics
item.description: Re:Lab AB is a Swedish company developing a chemical recycling solution for mixed plastic waste that cannot typically be recycled through conventional methods. By converting post-consumer plastics into renewable feedstocks for new chemical and plastic production, the company aims to reduce dependence on virgin fossil resources and prevent valuable materials from being incinerated or landfilled.

item.title: Building movements in the informal economy: Lessons for advancing labour rights in the circular economy
item.description: This briefing from Circle Economy and Women in Informal Employment Globalizing and Organizing (WIEGO) explores lessons from worker-led organising movements in informal economies across different countries and sectors.

item.title: Clothing the Footwear Loop
item.description: The “Closing the Footwear Loop” project is a major initiative led by Fashion for Good, bringing together 17 leading fashion and footwear brands and their existing circularity programs to tackle the complex challenges of circularity in the footwear industry. The project aims to transform the current linear “take-make-dispose” model into a circular one.
